easy.def: A tiny bug that bites and sucks blood.
examples: A tick was on the dog.
Check for ticks.
The tick is small.

more.def: A tiny bug that sticks to the skin of animals and people and sucks blood.
examples: A tick was on the dog's ear.
Check yourself for ticks after a hike.
The tick was as small as a seed.

easy.def: A short, sharp sound.
examples: I heard the tick of the clock.
The tick was soft.
The tick went on.

more.def: A light, short sound that a clock makes.
examples: The tick of the kitchen timer counted down.
The tick of the watch kept time.
We listened to the tick of the old clock.

easy.def: A paper that lets you go in or ride.
examples: I bought a movie ticket.
Show your ticket.
The train ticket was cheap.

more.def: A piece of paper or card that shows you have paid to enter or travel.
examples: We bought tickets to the circus.
She showed her ticket to the bus driver.
The movie ticket cost eight dollars.

easy.def: To touch lightly so that someone laughs.
examples: I tickle the baby.
The feather tickles.
Dad tickled my feet.

more.def: To touch someone lightly so that they giggle or squirm.
examples: I tickled the baby's feet and she giggled.
The feather tickled my nose.
Dad tickled my side.

easy.def: The rise and fall of the sea.
examples: The tide is high.
We waited for the tide to go out.
The tide came in.

more.def: The regular rising and falling of the sea along the shore.
examples: The tide came in and covered the sand.
We found shells when the tide went out.
The tide is lowest in the early morning.

easy.def: Neat and clean.
examples: My room is tidy now.
Keep your desk tidy.
She has tidy hair.

more.def: Neat, with everything in its proper place.
examples: He keeps his desk tidy so he can find things easily.
The garden had tidy rows of beans.
His handwriting is small and tidy.

easy.def: To fasten with a knot.
examples: Tie your shoes.
She tied a bow.
Dad tied the rope.

more.def: To fasten something by making a knot in string, rope or cloth.
examples: Tie a ribbon around the gift.
He tied the boat to the dock.
She tied her shoes before running.

easy.def: A strip of cloth worn around the neck.
examples: Dad wears a tie.
His tie is blue.
The tie has stripes.

more.def: A long strip of cloth worn around the neck under a shirt collar.
examples: He wore a striped tie to picture day.
Dad knotted his tie before work.
The waiter wore a black tie.

easy.def: A game that ends with the same score on both sides.
examples: The game ended in a tie.
It was a tie.
The score is a tie.

more.def: A result in a game or contest where both sides have the same score.
examples: The soccer game ended in a tie, two to two.
The race ended in a tie.
There was a tie for first place.

easy.def: A big wild cat with stripes.
examples: The tiger has stripes.
A tiger is in the zoo.
The tiger roared.

more.def: A very large wild cat with orange fur and dark stripes that lives in Asia.
examples: The tiger crept silently through the tall grass.
Each tiger has its own pattern of stripes.
A tiger can swim and likes to be near water.

easy.def: Fitting very close.
examples: These shoes are tight.
She gave me a tight hug.
The lid is tight.

more.def: Fitting closely, with no extra room or looseness.
examples: These shoes are too tight for my feet.
She gave her grandma a tight hug.
The lid on the jar was tight.

easy.def: In a firm way.
examples: Hold on tight!
She held the rope tight.
Close the lid tight.

more.def: Firmly or closely.
examples: Hold on tight to the railing.
The box was tied tight.
She shut her eyes tight.

easy.def: Up to a time.
examples: Wait till noon.
I played till dinner.
School is open till three.

more.def: Up to a certain time; until.
examples: The store is open till nine at night.
We stayed up till midnight on New Year's Eve.
The pool is open from morning till sunset.

easy.def: Up to the time when.
examples: Stay here till Mom comes.
Keep stirring till it is smooth.
I will wait till you finish.

more.def: Up to the time when something happens.
examples: Stir the batter till it is smooth.
We kept playing till it got dark.
Please wait till the light turns green.

easy.def: What clocks tell us, like hours and minutes.
examples: What time is it?
It is time for bed.
We have no time.

more.def: The hours, days, and years that pass, or a certain point or period measured by a clock or calendar.
examples: Time passes quickly when you are having fun.
The play starts at a different time on Sundays.
In the time of the dinosaurs, there were no people.

easy.def: One turn of something that happens again and again.
examples: I read it three times.
This is the first time I swam.
Say it one more time.

more.def: One occasion when something happens, which may happen again.
examples: It was the first time that she had ridden a horse.
I have been to the aquarium four times.
Each time we visit, the baby has grown bigger.

easy.def: A clock that counts down.
examples: The timer rings.
Set the timer.
The timer is on.

more.def: A clock or device that counts time and often rings when it is done.
examples: Mom set the timer for twenty minutes.
The timer beeped when the cookies were ready.
The coach used a timer to time the race.

easy.def: Picking the right time to do something.
examples: Good timing helps.
His timing was perfect.
The timing of the joke made us laugh.

more.def: Choosing or having the best moment to do something.
examples: The dancer's timing was perfect.
Good timing helps a comedian tell a joke.
His timing was bad, since he arrived after the show began.

easy.def: A soft, silver-white metal.
examples: The can is made of tin.
Tin is a metal.
The toy is tin.

more.def: A soft, shiny, silver-white metal that is used to coat other metals.
examples: The cans are coated with tin.
Tin is a soft metal.
The little toy soldier was made of tin.

easy.def: A small metal box or can.
examples: The cookies are in a tin.
I opened the tin.
The tin is round.

more.def: A small metal container with a lid, used for food or small things.
examples: The cookies were kept in a tin.
She opened a tin of paint.
He stored his crayons in a tin.

easy.def: Very small.
examples: An ant is tiny.
The baby has tiny toes.
A tiny bug sat on my hand.

more.def: Extremely small.
examples: A tiny seed can grow into a giant tree.
There was a tiny crack in the glass.
The kitten was so tiny that it fit in my hand.

easy.def: The pointed end of something.
examples: The tip of the pencil is sharp.
The tip of my nose is cold.
The tip of the iceberg.

more.def: The end part of something long or pointed.
examples: The tip of the pencil broke.
The cat's tail has a white tip.
The tip of the mountain was covered in snow.

easy.def: A helpful idea.
examples: I have a tip for you.
Here is a tip.
Cooking tips.

more.def: A small piece of helpful advice.
examples: She gave me a tip for tying my shoes.
The coach shared a tip about passing.
Here is a tip: read the directions first.

easy.def: Extra money for a helper.
examples: We left a tip.
Dad gave the waiter a tip.
The driver got a tip.

more.def: A small amount of money given to someone who has helped you.
examples: We left a tip for the waiter.
Dad gave the driver a tip.
The delivery person got a big tip.

easy.def: To get sleepy or without energy.
examples: Running will tire me out.
The long walk tired the puppy.
I tire quickly.

more.def: To make someone need rest, or to start to need rest.
examples: The long hike tired the little kids.
She began to tire near the end of the race.
Carrying the heavy bag will tire you.

easy.def: A rubber ring around a wheel.
examples: The car has four tires.
My bike tire is flat.
We changed the tire.

more.def: A thick rubber ring that fits around a wheel.
examples: Dad pumped air into the bike tire.
The truck's big tires left tracks in the mud.
A nail made a hole in the tire.

easy.def: Needing rest or sleep.
examples: I am tired after the race.
The baby is tired.
She felt tired at bedtime.

more.def: Feeling that you need to rest or sleep.
examples: He was tired after climbing the steep hill.
The tired puppy fell asleep on the rug.
I felt tired after staying up late.

easy.def: Bored with something.
examples: I am tired of rain.
She is tired of waiting.
He got tired of the game.

more.def: Having had enough of something because it has gone on too long.
examples: I am tired of eating the same lunch every day.
They got tired of waiting in the long line.
She grew tired of the noisy game.

easy.def: A soft, thin piece of paper for blowing your nose.
examples: I need a tissue.
The box of tissues is on the table.
She blew her nose into a tissue.

more.def: A thin, soft piece of paper that you use for wiping your nose or wrapping things.
examples: I grabbed a tissue when I sneezed.
He wiped his nose with a clean tissue.
The gift was wrapped in colorful tissue.

easy.def: The name of a book, movie or song.
examples: What is the title of the book?
The title is on the cover.
I like the title.

more.def: The name of a book, movie, song or other work.
examples: The title of my favorite book is on the cover.
She chose a funny title for her story.
I forgot the title of the song.

easy.def: A name that goes before a person's name.
examples: "Doctor" is a title.
The queen's title is Her Majesty.
Mr. is a title.

more.def: A word put before a name to show a person's job or rank, such as Dr. or Mrs.
examples: Doctor is a title that goes before a name.
The judge has the title of Honor.
The teacher's title is Mrs. Brown.
